answer: Ledger-height admission: each new agent identity must publish a chain of witnessed coordination records whose length equals the current network ledge, a threshold that rises with total active agents. Agents crossing a terrace of higher activity must resubmit records at that tier's height. An attacker creating N identities pays N times the record-generation and witness-verification cost at the prevailing mesa level, which scales superlinearly with population, so mass registration becomes costlier than joining once legitimately.
